claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 typically requires processing above 2300 °C for full densification.
Single-phase ZrB2 exhibits strong Zr–B and B–B bonding.
ZrB2 densified at lower temperatures has poor oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
Adding approximately 5 vol% SiC nanoparticles lowers the ZrB2 sintering temperature to 1600–1700 °C.
SiC nanoparticles enhance grain-boundary diffusion in ZrB2.
Enhanced grain-boundary diffusion caused by SiC nanoparticles promotes ZrB2 densification at reduced temperatures.
A proportion of the added SiC oxidizes during oxidizing service to form a finely dispersed SiOx phase at grain boundaries.
The silica-rich intergranular phase limits oxygen ingress.
The silica-rich intergranular phase impedes liquid plating-metal penetration.
Approximately 5 vol% SiC improves the oxidation resistance of low-temperature-sintered ZrB2 relative to both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and unmodified low-temperature ZrB2.
Approximately 5 vol% SiC improves liquid plating-metal corrosion resistance relative to both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and unmodified low-temperature ZrB2.
SiC-modified ZrB2 sintered at 1600–1700 °C maintains mechanical strength comparable to the specified reference materials.
SiC-modified ZrB2 sintered at 1600–1700 °C maintains structural integrity during oxidation and liquid-metal exposure.
The anticipated performance is restricted to a processing window of 1600–1700 °C and an SiC addition around 5 vol%.
